For the Informant : Mr. Vijayant Verma, Advocate  -----
04/16.05.2024 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the Stat  and learned counsel for the informant.
2.

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Mahila Thana P.S. Case No.05/2024,
registered for the alleged offence under Sections 376, 498A, 323, 306, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the Court of the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Ranchi.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner and informant were in relationship since 2010 and the allegations are also made that marriage was solemnized and the present FIR has been lodged on 06.01.2024.
He submits that the petitioner and informant were in live-in relationship.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer on the ground that the allegation under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code is also there.

5. Learned counsel for the informant submits that by way of alluring the informant, relationship was established and whenever she has tried to file complaint against the petitioner, she was stopped by the petitioner by way of allurement that he will purchase certain property in her favour.
6. Looking into the contents of the FIR, it transpires that the relationship was there since 2010 and Ravi Ranjan Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand ... Opposite ... on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21398915/

sentences.text: the FIR has been lodged on 06.01.2024.
In the FIR, the marriage is also said to be there between the parties and it has been pointed out that the petitioner and the informant were in live-in relationship.

Even if the argument of the learned counsel for the informant is accepted that the petitioner has stopped the informant to file the complaint on certain allurement, that cannot be a ground to reject the anticipatory bail application in a case where live-in relationship, prima facie, established.
7. In the attending facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the above-named petitioner is directed to surrender before the learned Court within three weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrender,
he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Ranchi in connection with Mahila Thana P.S. Case No.05/2024, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Ajay/
